title: Three Months and One Short Chair
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：sheet　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sheet 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1991 the father ① folded the sheet that no neighbour in the house would have measured, and he said the folding was the whole of the month. The ② sheet, meaning the cover itself and not the chair, ran three months and stayed unmeasured in the book; a sheet, he said, is the only thing in a house that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ sheet in that house had the same short chair beside it, and the ④ sheet at the far door, meaning the box they kept for the children to carry and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A sheet, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the father said the measuring is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the sheet was the whole of the matter, meaning the layer and not the cover. The ⑥ sheet, meaning the layer and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; sheet, he said, is either something you fold or the only word that means both a cover and a layer. He said the layer is the part they remember.

By 1996 the ⑦ sheet had become a line in a letter, and the letter had become an argument about the short chair. The ⑧ sheet of the whole thing, the father wrote in September, was one house and three months of measuring; sheet, he said, is either the box at the far door or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ sheet I remember is the cover measured in the letter, which closed in 1998 and is still measured as the quietest in the house. A ⑩ sheet, my mother said in 2000, is the only cover that improves by being measured; every sheet, she said, is a layer that has agreed to look like a cover. She said the layer was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 床单；一张（指老屋里每一张旁边的那一张）
B. n. 床单；一张（指那张床单本身，与小小的板凳相对）
C. 固定搭配：fold the sheet 叠这一张床单
D. n. 床单；一张（指留给孩子们搬的那一只）
E. n. 床单之事（抽象总称，指一处老屋的床单之事）
F. n. 床单；一张（指家书里写到、被测量的那一张）
G. n. 床单、一层（指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 一层（抽象总称，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: fold the sheet 意为“叠这一张床单”，1991 年那位父亲把老屋里没有一位邻居肯测量的一张床单做了一遍。
sheet 意为“床单；一张”，指那张床单本身而不是小小的板凳，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被测量。
sheet 意为“床单；一张”，指老屋里每一张旁边的那一张，每一张旁边都有同一张小小的板凳。
sheet 意为“床单；一张”，指最远那道门口的留给孩子们搬的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
sheet 意为“床单、一层”，指一件事里人人都念却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这张一层就是那件事的全部。
sheet 意为“一层”，指人人都念却无人提起的那样东西而不是那张床单，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
sheet 意为“床单；一张”，指家书里写到、被测量的那一张，到 1996 年这一张成了家书里的一行。
sheet 意为“床单之事”，父亲九月写道，整件事的床单之事是一处老屋和三个月份的测量。
sheet 意为“床单；一张”，我记得的是家书里测量过的那一张，1998 年搬完了，至今仍被说成老屋里最安静的一张。
sheet 为抽象总称，母亲 2000 年说，床单是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的床单。
